proposedchanges.title: Trump Imposes a 10% Aluminum Tariff Under Section 232
proposedchanges.description_long: On March 8, 2018, President Donald Trump issued Proclamation 9704 under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act, imposing a 10 percent tariff on covered aluminum imports. The administration said the tariff addressed a national-security risk found in a Commerce Department investigation. Section 232 lets a president adjust imports after a commerce secretary finds that they threaten national security. The proclamation made aluminum part of a wider dispute over steel, aluminum and trade policy. Tariffs apply at the border, but their economic effects depend on how companies adjust. Importers may absorb some costs, manufacturers may pay higher prices for material, or businesses may pass costs through to customers. The proclamation provides the rate and stated rationale, but that rationale is the administration’s position rather than an independent assessment of the threat. The order set the tariff but left its economic effects to subsequent market response.

evidencebasis: The original packet identifies Proclamation 9704 and the 10 percent rate. The latest descriptions provide the date, Section 232 authority, Commerce Department investigation, stated rationale, and possible cost distribution.
notes: The proposed long removes source-audit commentary while preserving the event's stated basis and limits. The American Presidency Project URL remains intact.
